title: The Old Stand
text: A stand of huge, straight trees rises taller than any tower, their bark silver and smooth, perfect timber. A ring of standing stones surrounds them, each carved with a face. All the faces are frowning, and none of the stones are mossy.

options.label: Fell the silver trees; timber like this would raise towers at home.

outcomes.text: You take a great deal of fine timber. The stone faces frown harder.
The stones were guarding the trees, and still are.

options.label: The wisest asks the stones' leave first, as the old folk would have.

outcomes.text: One tree is given freely, and the stone faces ease.

options.label: Take only the fallen wood, leaving the stones nothing to frown at.

outcomes.text: It is less, but no one minds. No stone turns to watch you go.
